_comment: Hand-written raw-spec.json, used by checks.resolve-import-lazy-lock's #47 case: local.nvim
here sets `dir` and deliberately does NOT set `dev` -- write `dev` too and this becomes the
same shape raw-spec.json's own local.nvim already covers. Reusing the existing raw-spec.json
would also mean touching golden/imported.plugins.json and the check's three counts of 19
(docs/plans/49-lazy-nvim-collision.md SS5.6 records the same trap), so this case gets its own
local.nvim carries `url`: without one, a routing regression would die on source.parse's
"has no url" before reaching the assertion this case actually wants, which is whether
classification 3L fires -- not a second way to fail on a missing url that
checks.extractor-local-dir already owns. It also carries the materialized
`defaults.version = "*"` (`versionFromDefaults = true`) that a routing regression would pin
from lazy-lock.json and then report as "is not validated"; that line's absence is itself part
of the assertion, not a semver-gate guard -- --import-lazy-lock seeds resolvedRef before #23's
gate runs, so the gate never fires here either way.
plain.nvim is copied verbatim from raw-spec.json's own entry: lazy-lock.json already has a
